spans.text: Beasts of Bestowal - known otherwise as eidolos - are beings that were granted a sacred order by an eidolic deity, and elevated to a more powerful, immortal, and eternal form. They are bound to perform the order they were given when elevated to their heightened state, but when it is complete they may find freedom.

The true body of a Beast of Bestowal is a crystal called sepherite, which contains their essence and a memory of what they are - their cosmogony. This crystal resides at the core of the Beast, and their body is a “projection of light” made from eidolic energy, which can be restored repeatedly if they are destroyed. This affords an eidolos a form of immortality, though powerful eidolic beings may be able to destroy their sepherite core.

When they exist for a long period of time without losing their physical form, the defeat of a Beast of Bestowal leads to them discarding their accumulated eidolic power in the form of a piece of equipment called an eidolic armament. This armament contains the instincts and a fragment of their power. The treasury section contains examples of the eidolic armaments of the Beasts in this section, as well as their sepherite cores.

Eidolos who have either completed their assigned task exhaustively, who were dismissed by their creator on good terms, or who were elevated by an eidolic deity that no longer exists or holds divinity may act as they wish, using their immortality as they see fit. Generally, these Beasts of Bestowal do not cause waves that might draw the attention of other eidolos or eidolic deities, as they may fear being permanently destroyed.

When an eidolos is killed, its body dissolves into nothingness, leaving only an eidolic armament and sepherite behind. This sepherite cannot be destroyed except by an eidolic deity, an eidolos of a higher cosmogony rank, or a resplendent constellequary (or by exceptionally powerful beings on par with these things).

3d4 hours after an eidolos is reduced to sepherite, it must attempt a Charisma saving throw with a DC equal to half the damage from the source that destroyed it (or 30 if it was an effect that instantly killed them). The DC decreases by 1 each time the eidolos fails it, and they re-attempt the saving throw every hour after failing. On a success, the eidolos regains its physical form with half of its maximum hit points restored.

is cast on the sepherite then its remaining time between checks is reset to 3d4 hours. The eidolos remains aware of everything happening around it while in sepherite form as though its senses were intact.
If an eidolos is killed by - but not permanently destroyed by - a constellequary, eidolic armament, or eidolic weapon, it loses its ability to restore itself for 1d10 x 10 years.
If an eidolos is permanently destroyed, any eidolic armament it left behind also crumbles into dust.
